newsitem.title: INDONESIA: JAKARTA CALL MONEY TRADED AT 14.5/15.0 PERCENT.
newsitem.headline: JAKARTA CALL MONEY TRADED AT 14.5/15.0 PERCENT.

text.p: Jakarta call money was traded at 14.5/15.0 percent on Monday morning on the back of sufficient liquidity supply, dealers said.
They said supply was adequate but further easing was limited by the central bank short-term certificate (SBI) rate, set artificially at a high level of 14.0 percent.
One local bank dealer said overnight rates at 18.0 percent could still be obtained in trades with small banks.
A balance of 579 billion rupiah was available to the market from maturing central bank papers on Monday.
The central bank continued its expensive rupiah policy for money of less than one-week to discourage dollar buying. The bank also closed the facility for short-term securities (SBPUs).
There was also no offer of repos on Monday. The bank cut all bilateral SBIs longer than one-week by 50 basis points last Friday after the foreign exchange market stabilised.
Dealers said the central bank was likely to extend its interest rate cut to money less than one-week once it was comfortable with the region's foreign exchange markets.

Bank Indonesia kept overnight SBIs at 14.0 percent, two-to-four day at 15.0 percent, one-week at 9.5 percent, two-week at 10.0, one-month at 10.625, three at 10.5, six at 11.125 and one-year at 11.75 percent.
Dealers said softer overnight rates drove longer-term rates in the interbank market lower. One-month was at 16.0/17.0 percent and three at 17.0/17.5 percent.
The average overnight interbank rate on Friday was 16.52 percent, compared with 17.05 percent on Thursday.
